newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends up, oil down on crush, exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends up, oil down on crush, exports.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended higher on Friday, propped up by explosive gains in soybeans, pit sources said.
Soyoil faltered, hit by lackluster USDA weekly export sales data and a weekly crush figure that came in well above trade expectations.

USDA Friday said U.S. net export sales of old crop soyoil during the week ended May 22 totaled 800 tonnes, below expectations for 4,000 to 6,000 tonnes. Soymeal sales totaled a minus 11,300 tonnes, well below expectations for 40,000 to 50,000 tonnes.
But new crop sales figures came in above expectations, suggesting to many that world buyers had enough supplies to tide them over until cheaper new crop supplies were available.
Soyoil was also hampered by the National Oilseed Processors Association's weekly crush tally of 25.462 million.
"There's some slack in the cash meal market," a trader said. "We could be overcrushed. We sure didn't need to put any more soyoil in the tanks. They're already pretty full."
Soymeal ended $2.40 to $1.00 per ton higher with July up $2.40 at $290.50 a ton. Soyoil ended 0.13 to 0.02 cent per lb lower with July off 0.10 at 23.78 cents.

While the active crush meant more supply of both soymeal and soyoil, trade sources said oil reacted more bearishly because demand for that commodity has been weaker. They said meal demand would likely be strong enough to soak up the extra supply but soyoil stockpiles would likely grow.

On the day, funds sold at least 1,400 lots soymeal and 1,000 lots soyoil, pit sources said. SAK Futures sold 700 lots July soymeal, Rosenthal Collins sold 300 July and FIMAT Futures sold 300 July and 100 August.
In soyoil, FIMAT and Iowa Grain each sold 300 July while Rand Financail, Refco Inc, Rosenthal Collins and Lee B. Stern each sold 200 July, traders said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 29,000 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 39,676 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 19,000 lots, against Thursday's 22,486 lots.
